lesson_title: Who Decides? The Three Economic Systems
hook_text: Every country on Earth has the same problem. Here are the three ways to solve it.
clip_script: Wants are unlimited. Resources are scarce. So every country must decide what to produce, how to produce it and for whom. There are three ways to decide. One: the state decides. It owns the land and the factories and writes a plan. That is a planned economy, the idea Karl Marx set out in 1848 and the Soviet Union tried from 1917. Equal, but full of queues and shortages. Two: buyers and sellers decide, through prices. That is a market economy, the idea Adam Smith described in 1776 as the invisible hand. Lots of choice, but nobody looks after those who cannot pay. Three: both decide. Private businesses do most of the producing, but the state runs Eskom and Transnet, builds schools and clinics, pays grants and makes rules. That is a mixed economy, and that is South Africa. Mixed does not mean half and half. It means both play a part.
visual_style: A whiteboard line from planned to market, with country flags placed along it; quick icons for a five-year plan, a market stall with price tags, and a split panel of a power station and a spaza shop.
pacing: Fast hook on scarcity, three equal beats for the systems, a slower landing on South Africa.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and place five countries on the line yourself.
